name: Fotoworkshop 'Alpenlicht'
beschreibung:
With its dramatic three-thousanders, roaring glacial streams, pristine mountain lakes like Lake Rifflsee and the expansive Mittelbergferner glacier, the Pitztal is one of the most stunning photographic regions in the Alps. A guided mountain photography workshop combines rugged nature with hands-on camera technique, showing participants how to capture high-contrast mountain light and dynamic alpine atmospheres.

Content & Formats

Workshops in the Pitztal are led by experienced alpine photographers (e.g., Mountain Moments, Martin Engelmann, and the Alpine Club Academy). Core topics include mastering the Golden Hour and Blue Hour, handling high-contrast light across glaciers and rocky ridges, shooting in manual mode (aperture, ISO, shutter speed), and RAW image workflows.

Special focus is placed on long exposure photography using circular polarizers and ND filters (e.g. ND64 or ND1000) to create silky-smooth water effects on mountain streams and waterfalls. Evening sessions cover post-processing in Adobe Lightroom Classic.

Rates & Duration: Single-day group workshops (7–8 hrs) run around €220–€250 per person. Two-day weekend intensives cost around €349–€390. Private 1:1 coaching starts around €280 for half a day or €490 for a full day.

Season: Summer season runs late June to mid-September with cable cars in full operation. Golden autumn (mid-September to late October) offers crystal-clear air and vibrant larch forests. Winter workshops on the Pitztal Glacier focus on snow, ice, and frozen formations.

Getting There

Main hubs include Arzl, Wenns, and Mittelberg/Mandarfen at the head of the valley. By car: A12 motorway to Imst/Pitztal, then follow the L16. By public transport: Train to Imst-Pitztal station, then VVT bus 210 to Mandarfen/Mittelberg. Regiobus travel is often included with the Pitztal Sommer Card.

Tips

  • Gear: Camera with manual controls, wide-angle and telephoto lenses, sturdy tripod, ND/polarizing filters, spare batteries, and weatherproof protection.
  • Fitness & Clothing: Sturdy hiking boots, layered weatherproof clothing. Standard fitness is sufficient for lift-accessed locations; basic mountain fitness required for hut trails.
  • Beginners: Introductory workshops welcome participants with no prior manual camera experience.
